entry.title: Designing a parking lot: the low-level design interview, explained
entry.summary:
Designing a parking lot: the low-level design interview, explained
"Design a parking lot" is the most common opener in a low-level design interview, and it is deceptively easy to start and surprisingly easy to fail. The trap is treating it as a coding problem — there is no algorithm to crack and no test cases to pass. What the round is really testing is object-oriented design: can you turn a fuzzy real-world problem into a clean set of classes, draw the relationships between them, decide where behaviour lives, and keep the design open to change when the interviewer adds a requirement five minutes in? The parking lot is a favourite precisely because everyone understands the domain, so there is nowhere to hide — the whole conversation is about the quality of your model. This guide walks th…
